title: Billing spike — all-hands talking points (scratch)
body:
Purpose:
Quick prep notes for an ad-hoc all-hands to explain yesterday's unexpected billing spike, reassure customers & internal teams, and lay out next steps. Working draft — keep short on-stage, deeper Q&A in post-all-hands thread.

TL;DR (3 lines)
- What happened: a billing multiplier bug in the token meter doubled billable tokens for ~2.5 hours for Hosted API customers.
- Impact: visible spike in usage-based invoices for a subset of accounts (primarily short-burst chat workloads). No data exposure.
- Status: patch deployed, rolling reconciliations started, customer support prioritized.

Notes to presenter (tone):
- Own it early: acknowledge clearly, avoid tech jargon up front.
- Reassure: refunds/reconciliations in progress, proactive outreach to impacted customers tonight.
- Emphasize improvement: this triggered an ops + billing instrumentation backlog item we are already addressing.

Suggested 60–90s script for CEO/Head of Product:
"Hi everyone — quick update on a billing issue some customers saw yesterday. We traced it to a token-metering multiplier introduced in a recent change, which overstated usage for a short window. No security or data problems. We moved fast to patch the code, start automatic refunds, and open a prioritized support lane. I know billing is sensitive; we’ll share a postmortem and concrete safeguards in the next 72 hours. Thank you to the engineers and CS folks who worked overnight."

Key technical bullet points (for follow-up / SRE):
- Root cause: regression in meter conversion step when seq_len < 32 AND quantization-cache enabled — multiplier applied twice.
- Blast window: 2026-03-09T21:14 to 2026-03-09T23:48 UTC (~2h34m).
- Affected cohort: ~1.8% of active hosted customers, generally small chat bursts (high short-message frequency).
- Mitigation: rollback + emergency patch rolled at 21:48 UTC; feature-flag added for safe deploys.
- Post-mitigation checks: synthetic traffic harness, top-100 customer invoice preview script.

Planned customer actions (customer-success playbook summary):
- Automated credit issuance: customers who saw >10% deviation will get credit equal to the overcharged amount.
- Outreach: Tier 1 customers (committed/Dedicated) get direct email/AM; Tier 2 targeted Slack/email templates.
- FAQ page: publish short FAQ & how-to-check your invoice steps.

Prep Q&A (anticipate these in all-hands and external comms):
Q: How do we know this won't recur?
A: We're shipping three layers of protection: unit tests for conversion logic, a billing-sanity monitor with anomaly alerts (per-customer rate + sudden multiplier detection), and production feature flagging for metering changes.

Q: Will customers be automatically refunded?
A: Yes — automated reconciliations are running. Manual review for borderline cases. Support will follow up with customers who prefer a manual explanation.

Q: Is any customer data at risk?
A: No. This is a billing calculation bug only; no data leak or model output corruption.

Q: How many customers impacted and financial scope?
A: ~1.8% of hosted customers; preliminary estimate < 0.2% of monthly revenue. Final reconciliation figures by EOD tomorrow.

Slack/Email post (short draft):
"Heads up: we patched a billing meter regression that caused inflated usage for a small number of Hosted API customers yesterday evening. Patch deployed; automated credits and direct outreach underway. Full postmortem + timeline will be shared in 72 hours. If you own customer comms or partner ops, check JIRA INC-2345 for playbook. — Anil"

Outstanding items / TODOs (owner tags):
- Finalize reconciliation script and run across last 60 days (Elliot)
- Draft customer FAQ + email templates (Priya)
- Postmortem doc + timeline + remediation roadmap (Sahana)
- Billing-monitoring alert dashboard: add multiplier anomaly rule (eng-metrics)
- Legal/finance review for complex invoices > $50k (Finance lead)

Metrics to show in all-hands slides (one slide, visual):
- Spike timeline (graph): token-rate vs baseline, annotate patch time.
- % customers affected and example invoice delta distribution (median, 90th pct).
- Latency/availability unaffected (confirm).

Follow-up comms cadence:
- Immediate: all-hands mention + internal Slack thread pinned.
- 24h: customer-facing FAQ + targeted outreach sent.
- 72h: full postmortem + remediation plan published.
- 14d: audit of billing systems + test coverage report.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep CEO script <90s. Avoid technical blame ("regression" OK).
- Put customer examples in appendix, anonymized.
- Confirm refund automation idempotency (avoid double-credit).
- Prep one-liner for investors if asked (ops issue, limited financial impact, full remediation).

End of draft — pull quotes for slides and Slack ready in separate small bullets if we want to reuse.
